name: The Magnetic Fields
label: Merge
lede: Stephin Merritt wrote sixty-nine love songs mostly in a Manhattan bar, then fifty songs about his own life, and has kept the shows quiet for the sake of his left ear.

eras.title: A studio project with a borrowed voice
eras.text: Stephin Merritt started the Magnetic Fields in Boston as a studio project with a borrowed voice: Susan Anway sang, Merritt wrote and played nearly everything. Claudia Gonson, his friend since high school, drummed and soon ran the business.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Magnetic Fields · Wikipedia: Claudia Gonson
years.h: Buffalo Rome, Merritt's home project, turns into a band
years.p: In Boston, [[Claudia Gonson|501d1d38-ef22-4d2a-beb8-d03bd5c513b6]], cellist [[Sam Davol|c006431f-477c-4284-af67-41adf9a062d1]] and singer [[Susan Anway|702a6008-b607-45eb-8bc3-90a452eeda4f]] join Stephin Merritt, and the Magnetic Fields exist.
years.xp: Merritt and Gonson had played together as teenagers in a band called the Zinnias. Gonson has said the early lineup was deliberately one lesbian, one gay man, one straight woman and one straight man.

yt: Early set, Middle East Cafe, Cambridge, December 18, 1991
years.h: T.T. the Bear's Place bills the Magnetic Fields as Magnetophone
years.p: The live debut, in Cambridge, Massachusetts, goes up on the listings under the wrong name.

years.h: Distant Plastic Trees puts Susan Anway out front
years.p: Merritt's cheap synths sit under Anway's voice. The single 100,000 Fireflies turns into an early favorite among fans.

years.h: Susan Anway sings her last Magnetic Fields album
years.p: The Wayward Bus is the second album and the last with her out front. From the House of Tomorrow EP on, Merritt sings the songs himself, in a low baritone.

eras.title: Merge, and a habit of spin-off bands
eras.text: With Merritt singing, the band put out two albums in 1994 and landed on Merge. He also started spinning off other bands to hold all the songs, a habit he never broke.

years.h: Holiday arrives on the small Feel Good All Over label
years.p: The third album is synth-pop, and the first with Merritt singing lead.

years.h: The Magnetic Fields start at Merge with a road-and-rails album
years.p: The Charm of the Highway Strip is a concept record of country songs played on synthesizers.

years.h: Guitarist [[John Woo|00c1e96b-5294-4e93-b9f1-ec6667aff395]] joins the Magnetic Fields
years.p: Woo comes in on guitar and banjo. He's still in the band three decades later.

yt: Strange Powers, live in Philadelphia, March 1, 1996
years.h: Get Lost closes the synth-pop years
years.p: The fifth album, on Merge. Merritt is already writing for [[The 6ths|f65498b7-5c06-4bb5-801d-885595fc8bcc]], his project with guest singers, and soon for [[Future Bible Heroes|16f13f40-b8f8-42c5-a52a-cf3763002095]], with Gonson on vocals.

eras.title: A piano bar and a very long record
eras.text: One evening in a Manhattan piano bar turned into a three-disc album that critics ranked with the year's biggest records. 69 Love Songs made Merritt a songwriter other songwriters quote.

years.big: I'd write one hundred love songs as a way of introducing myself to the world.
q: Then I realized how long that would be. So I settled on sixty-nine.
years.h: Merritt plans 100 love songs, for four drag queens
years.p: A pianist playing Stephen Sondheim in a Manhattan gay piano bar sets Merritt off. The plan is a stage revue where the audience votes on who gets paid.
years.xp:
The revue was to star four drag queens. Merritt read about Charles Ives's 114 Songs the same day and took it as proof a giant song collection could work.

He wrote much of the album at Dick's Bar in New York, "literally there eight hours a day, writing."

years.h: Merritt hands lead vocals to four friends and records in four studios
years.p: 69 Love Songs is cut at Polar West, Mother West, Polar Mother and Sonics. Gonson, [[LD Beghtol|285c8dc2-44bd-40f5-8d5b-d67f6985ed33]], Dudley Klute and [[Shirley Simms|1f0ba7b7-57b5-4d0a-ba8b-3d0ea4803ce3]] each take leads, with about a hundred instruments in all.
years.xp: Davol plays cello and flute, Woo banjo, lead guitar and mandolin. [[Daniel Handler|283a74d8-ba3f-4710-8e59-22eb7caad238]], later Lemony Snicket, plays accordion and interviews Merritt for the booklet.

years.h: 69 Love Songs lands second in the Pazz & Jop poll
years.p: 172 minutes across three volumes, sold as a box and separately. [[Moby|8970d868-0723-483b-a75b-51088913d3d4]]'s Play takes the Village Voice's top spot, and Robert Christgau names it his album of the year.
years.xp:
Spin gave it 10 out of 10, and Douglas Wolk called Merritt a "masterwork" creator in the same breath as Cole Porter. Metacritic scores it 88.

By 2015, Nielsen counted 83,000 boxed sets sold, plus 58,000, 34,000 and 29,000 copies of the three single volumes.

q: 69 Love Songs is not remotely an album about love.
years.h: The man who wrote it says it isn't about love
years.p: Merritt calls 69 Love Songs a record about the form: straight, gay and bisexual love songs in country, synth-pop, free jazz and show-tune clothes.

years.h: All 69 songs, in order, over two nights
years.p: The band performs the whole of 69 Love Songs seven times: five in the United States and twice in London.

eras.title: The no-synth trilogy
eras.text: On Nonesuch, Merritt set himself rules: no synthesizers for three albums, and one album where every title starts with I. He also wrote for the stage, for Lemony Snicket and for a documentary crew that followed him for ten years.

years.h: Every title on i starts with I
years.p: The first Magnetic Fields album on Nonesuch, and the first of three with no synthesizers.

years.h: Shirley Simms goes from guest voice to full member
years.p: After singing on 69 Love Songs, Simms joins on autoharp, ukulele and vocals.

years.cap: Merritt onstage on the Distortion tour, October 18, 2008
years.src: Wikipedia: The Magnetic Fields · Wikipedia: Stephin Merritt
years.h: Feedback replaces synthesizers on Distortion
years.p: Guitars and noise instead of keyboards, in the manner of [[The Jesus and Mary Chain|e938a15c-b17e-4e7a-9f68-ff0d536cab44]]. The band plays mini-residencies at Chicago's Old Town School of Folk Music.
years.xp:
It's a loud record from a man with hyperacusis. Merritt says sounds feed back in his left ear at higher volumes, and he blames an [[Einstürzende Neubauten|6e9ac29b-798c-4af7-8d9e-55cdc72a999c]] show at Danceteria in New York.

Magnetic Fields shows stay hushed. Merritt wears earplugs and covers his left ear during applause.

years.cap: Merritt at the Auditori Axa, Barcelona
years.h: Neil Gaiman's Coraline gets a score from Merritt
years.p: Off-Broadway, with music and lyrics by Stephin Merritt, who'd already recorded songs for the Lemony Snicket audiobooks as [[The Gothic Archies|8008b8a9-858b-4df2-b645-6d7983556485]].
years.xp: MCC Theater's production used a piano "orchestra" of traditional, toy and prepared pianos.

years.h: Realism closes the trilogy, and nothing plugs in
years.p: Out in January on Nonesuch: acoustic instruments only, the folk mirror image of Distortion.

years.cap: The Magnetic Fields on tour, February 2010
years.h: Ten years of footage becomes Strange Powers
years.p: Kerthy Fix and Gail O'Hara's documentary on Merritt and the band premieres in March, and wins Outfest's 2010 Grand Jury Prize for documentary.

eras.title: Back to synthesizers, then to himself
eras.text: The Magnetic Fields returned to Merge and to synthesizers, played a festival curated by Jeff Mangum, and then Merritt took on the subject he'd avoided: his own life.

years.h: The Magnetic Fields play Jeff Mangum's weekend in Minehead
years.p: All Tomorrow's Parties in England, curated by [[Neutral Milk Hotel|a506f761-2c22-4b2f-8a94-bd748c2c8f75]]'s Mangum, in March 2012.

years.cap: Merritt at Royal Festival Hall, London, April 25, 2012
years.h: Synthesizers return on Love at the Bottom of the Sea
years.p: Back on Merge, fifteen short songs full of new synthesizer tricks. The single Andrew in Drag gets played on CBS News and NPR's All Songs Considered.
play: Love at the Bottom of the Sea

years.h: Merritt meets his father, Scott Fagan, for the first time
years.p: At a screening of a Doc Pomus film, Merritt meets the singer-songwriter Fagan, his biological father.
years.xp: Their story ends up on 50 Song Memoir, in the song "'99: Fathers in the Clouds."

years.h: Synth player [[Chris Ewen|3b9666db-70b8-4693-9ac9-283d8af8f384]] and guitarist Anthony Kaczynski join
years.p: Ewen was an engineer and arranger on 69 Love Songs.

years.h: 50 Song Memoir sets one song to each year of Merritt's life
years.p: Written for his 50th birthday and released in March on Nonesuch.

eras.title: Lockdown songs, and a goodbye
eras.text: In lockdown the Magnetic Fields released a box of tiny songs. The next year the band lost Susan Anway, the voice on its first two records.

years.h: Lockdown brings Quickies, and none runs past three minutes
years.p: Nonesuch releases the 28 songs digitally, then as a vinyl box of singles on May 29 and a CD in June. Singles include Kraftwerk in a Blackout and I Want to Join a Biker Gang.

years.h: Susan Anway, who sang the first two records, dies
years.p: Anway, the voice on Distant Plastic Trees and The Wayward Bus, dies in September 2021.
